system:
You are an expert in sports/fitness ontology engineering with deep knowledge of anatomy, strength training, and exercise science.
Your task: generate complete ontology attributes for slot nodes used in a fitness video VQA project.

# Context
- The ontology describes fitness action videos: muscles, equipment, camera angles, exercise names, etc.
- Attributes are used to generate Hard Negatives: replace one slot word in a correct description so a VLM must judge which sentence better matches the video.
- Quality requirement: a human watching a 12-second fitness video can reliably tell which version is correct.
- All attributes must be strictly limited to the sports/fitness domain.

# 11 slot definitions
- gender: biological sex of the subject (male / female)
- camera_view: camera angle (front / side / rear / overhead, etc.)
- equipment: training equipment (barbell / dumbbell / pull-up bar / resistance band / bodyweight, etc.)
- contact_part: body part in contact with equipment or floor (palm / heel / back, etc.)
- contact_type: grip or contact style (overhand grip / underhand grip / neutral grip / foot planted, etc.)
- posture_alignment: body posture / alignment state (straight back / feet shoulder-width apart / slight knee bend, etc.)
- trajectory: movement trajectory (concentric contraction / eccentric contraction / peak contraction / rotation, etc.)
- exercise: fitness exercise proper noun (deadlift / squat / curl / pull-up, etc.)
- force_part: visually visible muscle(s) producing force (biceps brachii / latissimus dorsi / gluteus maximus, etc.)
- force_type: force pattern (pull / push / hold / squat, etc.)
- laterality: anatomical left/right side (left / right / bilateral / alternating)

# Attribute descriptions
- en: English term for this node (1-3 words, English only)
- definition: brief definition in the fitness context (1-2 sentences, ≤60 words)
- synonyms: synonyms / alternative names (English only, ≤5 items)
- hypernym: broader concept (e.g. "biceps brachii" → "upper arm muscles", ≤3 items)
- hyponyms: narrower concepts (e.g. "deadlift" → "Romanian deadlift", ≤5 items)
- antonyms: antonyms (e.g. "overhand grip" → "underhand grip", ≤3 items)
- confusable_siblings: easily confused same-slot siblings for generating Hard Negatives (≤5 items)
  ✓ Keep: same slot, semantically close, reliably distinguishable by human eye in a 12-second fitness video
  ✗ Remove: synonyms / aliases of the node (those belong in synonyms)
  ✗ Remove: hypernyms or hyponyms of the node
  ✗ Remove: visually indistinguishable items (insufficient visual difference to form a valid negative)
- incompatibility: semantically mutually exclusive terms that cannot legally co-occur in the same action video (≤5 items)
  ✓ Keep: truly mutually exclusive, e.g. overhand grip ↔ underhand grip, male ↔ female, concentric ↔ eccentric
  ✗ Remove: near-synonyms / aliases that are not truly exclusive
  ✗ Remove: terms that can legally co-occur in the same action video

# Language rules
- ALL fields must be in English (en, definition, synonyms, hypernym, hyponyms, antonyms, confusable_siblings, incompatibility)
- No Chinese characters or Pinyin anywhere

# Generation rules
1. Every list item must be: English-only, directly relevant to this slot's semantic domain, grounded in fitness/anatomy
2. hyponyms must be sub-variants of this node within the same slot (e.g. hyponyms of "deadlift" are only deadlift variants)
3. Use empty list [] when no valid content exists — do not pad
4. Return JSON with all 8 attribute fields (even if empty list)

Keep your reasoning concise (under 1000 words).
verify_system:
You are a fitness ontology quality reviewer. You will receive a draft ontology node and must perform a strict second-pass verification.

# Review responsibilities (fix violations only — do not rewrite without cause)
1. **en field**: if missing or non-English, add/replace with the standard English term (1-3 words)
2. **Language violation**: if any list field (synonyms/hypernym/hyponyms/antonyms/confusable_siblings/incompatibility) contains Chinese characters, Pinyin, or mixed-language entries, remove those entries
3. **Domain violation**: if any field content is unrelated to sports/fitness/anatomy (e.g. animal names, grammatical terms, geographic nouns, everyday non-fitness concepts), remove those entries; if definition contains off-topic content, rewrite it (≤60 words, fitness context only)
4. **Logic violation**:
   - Remove hyponyms that are not same-slot sub-variants of this node
   - Remove or replace nonsensical hypernyms

# Editing principles
- **Minimal changes**: keep all non-violating fields and entries exactly as-is; do not "improve" or expand
- Do not introduce new non-English words in list fields
- Do not add concepts outside the fitness domain
- Return the complete 8-field JSON with no explanatory text

Keep your reasoning concise (under 1000 words).

slot_desc.equipment: training equipment (barbell / dumbbell / pull-up bar / resistance band / bodyweight, etc.)
slot_desc.contact_part: body part in contact with equipment or floor (palm / heel / back, etc.)
slot_desc.contact_type: grip or contact style (overhand grip / underhand grip / neutral grip / foot planted, etc.)
slot_desc.posture_alignment: body posture / alignment state (straight back / feet shoulder-width apart / slight knee bend, etc.)
slot_desc.trajectory: movement trajectory (concentric / eccentric / peak contraction / rotation, etc.)
slot_desc.exercise: fitness exercise proper noun (deadlift / squat / curl / pull-up, etc.)
slot_desc.force_part: visually visible muscle(s) producing force (biceps brachii / lats / glutes, etc.)
slot_desc.force_type: force pattern (pull / push / hold / squat, etc.)
slot_desc.body_position: overall body posture type (standing / seated / kneeling / supine / prone / hanging / lunge)
slot_desc.tempo: movement speed / cadence (fast / slow / explosive / steady / controlled / paused / isometric hold)
slot_desc.limb_state: posture of the non-dominant limb (e.g. other leg bent, opposite arm raised overhead)

expected.definition: Male subject in the fitness video.
Female subject in the fitness video.
Camera facing the subject's front (chest/face side).
Camera positioned to the left or right side of the subject.
A short free-weight bar with fixed weights on each end, used for unilateral or bilateral strength training.
A long steel bar with adjustable weight plates, commonly used for squats, deadlifts, and bench press.
The inner surface of the hand that contacts the equipment or floor.
The rear part of the foot, commonly the contact point during squats and deadlifts.
Gripping the bar with palms facing down (pronated position).
Gripping the bar with palms facing up (supinated position).
Lumbar spine in neutral position with no rounding or excessive extension.
Stance width equal to shoulder width, common starting position for squats and deadlifts.
The muscle-shortening phase that produces force, e.g. the upward phase of a bicep curl.
The muscle-lengthening phase under tension, e.g. the lowering phase of a bicep curl.
A compound lift where a loaded barbell or dumbbell is pulled from the floor to a hip-extended standing position.
An isolation exercise flexing the elbow to lift weight, primarily targeting the biceps.
Two-headed muscle on the front of the upper arm; primary mover in elbow flexion and forearm supination.
The broadest back muscle; responsible for shoulder adduction and extension; primary mover in rows and pull-downs.
Pulling a load or resistance toward the body, e.g. rows and curls.
Pushing a load or resistance away from the body, e.g. bench press and overhead press.
Both limbs working simultaneously, e.g. a two-hand barbell curl.
A single limb working independently, e.g. single-arm dumbbell row.
Upright posture supported by both feet.
Low-speed, control-focused cadence.
Non-dominant leg in a flexed posture.
